faqs.question: How is migraine different from a regular headache?
faqs.answer: Migraine is a neurological condition, not just a bad headache. It typically involves moderate to severe throbbing pain (usually on one side), nausea or vomiting, sensitivity to light and sound, and can last 4–72 hours. Some people experience aura — visual disturbances, tingling, or speech changes before the headache starts. Dr. Yuvraj Lahre can accurately diagnose whether your headaches are migraines and provide migraine-specific treatment.
